title: Hand over a town LoRa mesh: logbook, backups and spares
summary: Make a town LoRa mesh something the next person can run when the builder is gone. Keep a logbook, a map and a card for every relay, back up settings and keys safely, keep spares loaded and ready, look after the power through the seasons, and keep an offline kit for rebuilding without the internet.

materials.item: Laptop or small computer with the Meshtastic command-line tool, and a USB data cable (charge-only cables carry no data)
Binder, printed town map, site cards, pencils and coloured pens
USB sticks for the offline kit and the config backups, and envelopes to seal the backups in
Spare board of each type in use, on the town's firmware, region set, and loaded from a relay's backup with its private and public key lines deleted
Spare tuned antenna and a coax jumper with connectors
Spare fuses of each rating used at the sites
Spare charged battery of the type used at the sites
Self-amalgamating tape and sealant for coax joints

steps.text: Start the logbook: a printed binder at the hub and the same files on the hub or NOMAD box. Write the town settings sheet: region US, preset, channel names, hop limit, firmware version, and who holds the admin keys.
Mark every relay, home base and the hub on a printed town map, and fill in a site card for each relay (template in the notes). For MeshCore relays, see MeshCore differences in the operations guide.

Back up every relay while connected by USB or Bluetooth: meshtastic --export-config > relay-name.yaml. Save the channel set with meshtastic --qr-all (it prints the URL; the QR needs the pyqrcode package from "meshtastic[cli]"). Put the files and a printed QR on two USB sticks, in sealed, dated envelopes kept in two places.
steps.warn: The backup holds the node's private key, its admin keys and every channel key. Never send it over the mesh or leave it on a shared computer.

steps.text: Replace a dead relay with the pre-loaded spare and check it is heard from the ground. Add its new node ID as a favourite wherever the old one was, remove the old ID, test remote admin, and update the card, map and logbook.
steps.warn: Fit the antenna before the spare gets power: transmitting without one can damage the radio. Never power two boards that carry the same keys.

steps.text: Each season, check power: dawn voltage against last year's, snow and shade on panels, battery age, damp in boxes. Sizing and cold-charging limits are in the town mesh guide.
steps.warn: A swollen, leaking or hot lithium battery is finished and can catch fire: take it out of service.

steps.text: Keep the offline kit current: firmware zips for every board in use, the app, the command-line tool and its wheels, every backup, and this guide. Twice a year, have the next keeper restore a backup onto a bench node and run the traceroute survey using only the binder.

## The network logbook

A printed binder at the hub, and the same files on the hub or NOMAD box:

1. **Town settings:** region (US), preset, channel names and indexes, hop limit, firmware version, who holds admin keys, date of each change.
2. **Topology map:** a printed town map with every relay, home base and the hub; a line for every working link with its SNR both ways and the date, from traceroutes; weak links in another colour.
3. **A site card per relay** (below), in map order.
4. **Visit log:** date, who, what was done, readings.
5. **Check sheet:** each relay's last-heard time, voltage, ChUtil and AirUtilTX, weekly.
6. **How-to:** this guide, and where the offline kit and sealed envelopes are.

## Site card

One per relay, in pencil, updated at every visit.

```

```

## Backup and restore

Connect by USB or Bluetooth: the command-line tool will not export or configure a remote node (Meshtastic CLI source).

- Back up: `meshtastic --export-config > relay-north.yaml`. On Windows PowerShell 5.1 the `>` sign can write the file in UTF-16, which `--configure` can't read. Use `meshtastic --export-config relay-north.yaml` there: CLI 2.7.11 writes the file itself, in UTF-8.
- Restore: `meshtastic --configure relay-north.yaml`. It also puts back the file's admin keys, so export again after any change to settings or admin keys. A board that is erased and comes back with new keys keeps its node ID, and nodes that remember its old key drop its NodeInfo: restore its own file, or have them run `--remove-node` on it (Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp).
- Channel set as URL and QR code: `meshtastic --qr-all` (Meshtastic CLI usage)

The file holds the names, channel URL, fixed position, device and module settings, and the security section: the node's private and public keys and its admin keys. It does not hold the node list or favourites (Meshtastic CLI source): keep favourites on the site card and set them again with `meshtastic --set-favorite-node '!a1b2c3d4'`. The node only marks a favourite it already has in its list. If it hasn't heard that node yet, nothing happens and no error shows: look for `*` in the Fav column of `meshtastic --nodes` (Meshtastic CLI source, Meshtastic AdminModule.cpp).

**Keep it secret.** The channel URL and QR carry the channel names, keys and LoRa settings, and holding a channel's key lets you read it (Meshtastic joining). The private key must stay confidential (Meshtastic security). The file also holds any Wi-Fi and MQTT passwords set on the node (Meshtastic CLI source). Never send them over the mesh or leave them on a shared computer: keep them, with the printed QR, on two USB sticks in sealed, dated envelopes in two places. The binder says only where.

**Admin keys.** A relay takes settings over the air only from up to three admin public keys (Meshtastic security, Meshtastic remote admin). The remote admin page lists only `--get` and `--set` over the air, for example `meshtastic --dest '!a1b2c3d4' --get lora.region` (Meshtastic remote admin). The tool's source also sends `--set-favorite-node` and `--remove-node` to a `--dest` node, but test those on a bench pair before you rely on them (Meshtastic CLI source). Give the slots to two people's handhelds and the hub node, and back those up too: each file holds the private key matching the admin key on every relay. `--set security.admin_key` adds a key and `0` clears the list; one key can't be removed alone (Meshtastic remote admin). Over the air, clear and re-add in one command, for example `meshtastic --dest '!a1b2c3d4' --set security.admin_key 0 --set security.admin_key "base64:KEY1" --set security.admin_key "base64:KEY2"`, then test with `--get lora.region`. Clearing alone cuts your own access, and the relay then needs a visit. Lose every admin device and its backup, and each relay must be changed on site, plugged in. Leave Managed Mode off: remote admin works without it (Meshtastic remote admin). With it on, the node ignores settings sent from an app over USB, Bluetooth or Wi-Fi too, so only an admin-key message over the air can change it. If the admin devices are lost, you would have to erase and reflash the node (Meshtastic security, Meshtastic AdminModule.cpp).

**Loading a spare.** Set the spare's region first: that makes its own key pair (Meshtastic security). Copy the relay's file, delete its `privateKey` and `publicKey` lines, and `--configure` the spare with the copy: it keeps its own keys and takes the relay's settings and admin keys (Meshtastic CLI source). Then check that `meshtastic --get security.public_key` on the spare differs from the relay's (Meshtastic remote admin). Never run two boards with the same keys: a node that hears its own public key from another device warns that the key may be compromised (Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp).

## Replacing a node

**Spares kit, per board type:** a spare board on the town's firmware, loaded as above and labelled; a tuned antenna; a coax jumper; fuses; a charged battery; tape and sealant; a USB data cable.

A replacement is a new node to the mesh: a new node ID, taken from its chip's MAC address (Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp), and its own keys. From firmware 2.8 the ID comes from the key instead (Meshtastic security), so check this step before you upgrade. So:

- Add the new ID as a favourite wherever the old one was: CLIENT_BASE nodes and zero-cost hops between routers both work from favourites (Meshtastic roles, Meshtastic zero-cost hops). Also on your handhelds and the hub. Do it after the new node has been heard: it sends its NodeInfo about 30 s after it starts, a node can only favourite a node already in its list, and zero-cost hops need the favourite's role known too. Look for `*` in the Fav column of `--nodes` (Meshtastic NodeInfoModule.cpp, Meshtastic Router.cpp, Meshtastic AdminModule.cpp).
- Remove the old ID from the node lists you look after: `meshtastic --remove-node '!oldid'` (Meshtastic CLI source).
- A relay's admin keys came with its backup: test remote admin from the ground before you leave. If the dead node was an admin device, its new key is on no relay and its old key still fills a slot. From another admin device, clear and re-add each relay's list in one command, as under Admin keys (Meshtastic remote admin).
- Update the card, map and log; take the dead node to the bench.

## Power through the seasons

Battery and panel sizing, cold-charging limits and boxes are in the power sections of [the town mesh guide](#guides/build_lora_town_mesh). Each year:

- **Before freeze-up:** dawn voltage against last year's, clean panels, check the low-temperature charge cut-off, replace weak or swollen cells, log install dates.
- **Winter:** dawn voltage weekly; clear snow from panels you can reach safely.
- **Spring and summer:** boxes for damp, vents, glands, coax tape; box heat in afternoon sun.

## Offline kit

On two USB sticks and on the hub or NOMAD box:

- Firmware zips for each chip family in use, of the release the town runs. For 2.7.26: ESP32-S3 170 MB, nRF52840 46 MB, ESP32 41 MB, RP2040 3 MB; the debug-elfs zips aren't needed (Meshtastic firmware releases). Keep the previous release too, in case a new one misbehaves. A roll back is not documented: back up every relay before an upgrade, and try a roll back on a bench board first.
- The Android .apk, the command-line tool and esptool as a folder of Python wheels (on a computer with the same operating system and Python version as the offline one, run `pip wheel esptool "meshtastic[cli]" -w wheels`, then try `pip install --no-index --find-links wheels esptool "meshtastic[cli]"` once with the network off; `pip download` alone fetches source-only esptool 5 and pyqrcode, which need setuptools to install; Python 3 must already be on the offline computer), nRF52 bootloaders and the factory-erase .uf2 files (the Meshtastic_nRF52_factory_erase_v3 file in the firmware download must match the SoftDevice named in the board's INFO_UF2.TXT, 7.3.0 or 6.1.0, or the board may need a hardware programmer; meshtastic_factory_erase.uf2 from the bootloader release works only if INFO_UF2.TXT has a Factory-Erase line): "Flashing with no internet" in [the node guide](#guides/build_lora_node).
- Every relay's backup goes on the two sealed sticks only: never on the NOMAD box or any computer others can use, because each file holds private keys and the channel keys. This guide, both build guides and the bands card go on both.
